# `services`

::: info
Анықтаманың өзі ағылшын тілінде: ол WIT файлдарынан автоматты түрде жасалады.
:::

Cross-mod services (shape only in 0.1; implemented since 0.2; across the network since 0.3.1). A provider declares the service in `mod.toml` `[provides]` and registers it with `provide`. Consumers call it by name and a semver requirement; the host picks the highest compatible provider, converts values and calls the provider's `guest.call-service`. The SDK turns the provider's WIT into typed stubs, so authors rarely use `call` directly. Rules: a consumer may only call providers it depends or soft-depends on. Calls are synchronous; a call that would re-enter a mod already on the call stack (A -&gt; B -&gt; A) fails with `reentrant`. Players inside values are host handles `{"$h": n}`; a handle of a player who left is stale. (0.3.1) Remote calls: a client mod can call a service a server mod provides, and a server mod one a client mod provides, over the 0xBC `SERVICE_CALL` / `SERVICE_RESULT` ops. They are asynchronous: `call-remote` returns a call id at once and the answer arrives later as the custom event `<mod-id>:service-result` to the calling mod (subscribe with `events.subscribe-custom`). The payload is a canonical CBOR map `{"id": call-id, "ok": true, "value": <result>}` or `{"id": call-id, "ok": false, "error": {"kind": <kind>, "message": <text>}}`. The kinds are `not-found`, `version-mismatch`, `not-permitted`, `busy`, `provider-error`, `trap`, `bad-value`, `too-large`, `internal` (the other side's answer) and `unavailable`, `timeout`, `disconnected` (decided locally). The event reaches exactly one handler call per remote call, also for failures that are known at once (`unavailable`), and never during the `call-remote` that caused it. Calling needs the `channels` permission. The providing side decides what may be called: only services declared with `remote = true` in `mod.toml` `[provides]` (optionally limited to `remote-methods`) are reachable, every caller peer has a rate limit, and the provider runs under its normal time budget. Inside the provider, `caller` tells who called.

Package `blockheads:api@0.3.1` · Lua table `bh.services` · [WIT source](https://github.com/Blockheads-Club/mod-sdk/blob/dev/wit/blockheads-api/services.wit)

## Types

### `call-error` <Badge type="info" text="variant" />

Why a service call failed.

| Case | Payload | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `not-found` | – | No provider with that name is loaded. |
| `version-mismatch` | – | Providers exist but none matches the version requirement. |
| `not-permitted` | – | The caller does not depend (or soft-depend) on the provider, or the method is admin-only. |
| `reentrant` | – | The call would re-enter a mod that is already on the call stack (A -&gt; B -&gt; A). |
| `provider-error` | `string` | The provider returned an error; the payload is its message. |
| `trap` | – | The provider trapped or ran over its time budget. |
| `bad-value` | `string` | Arguments or result were not valid canonical CBOR for the method. |

### `remote-target` <Badge type="info" text="variant" />

(0.3.1) Where a remote call goes.

| Case | Payload | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `server` | – | The server (from a client mod). |
| `player` | `borrow<player>` | One player's client (from a server mod). |

### `call-id` <Badge type="info" text="type" />

```txt
type call-id = u32;
```

(0.3.1) Identifies an open remote call; the `service-result` event carries it back.

### `remote-caller` <Badge type="info" text="record" />

(0.3.1) Who made the remote call that `call-service` is serving.

| Field | Type | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `mod-id` | `mod-id` | The mod that called, on the other side. |
| `player` | `option<player>` | The calling player when a client called this server mod; none when the server called this client mod. |

## Functions

### `provide` <Badge type="info" text="function" />

```txt
provide: func(name: string, version: string) -> result<_, api-error>;
```

Registers the calling mod as provider of `name` at `version` (semver). Must match `mod.toml`.

### `call` <Badge type="info" text="function" />

```txt
call: func(name: string, version-req: string, method: string, args: value) -> result<value, call-error>;
```

Calls `method` of the best provider matching `version-req` (a semver requirement such as `^1.1`). `args` is a canonical CBOR array of the method's parameters.

### `call-remote` <Badge type="info" text="function" />

```txt
call-remote: func(to: remote-target, name: string, version-req: string, method: string, args: value, timeout-ms: u32) -> result<call-id, api-error>;
```

(0.3.1) Calls `method` of the best provider matching `version-req` on the other side. `args` is a canonical CBOR array of at most 32 KiB. `timeout-ms` is how long to wait for the answer: 0 means 5000, the largest is 30000. Fails at once with `invalid-argument` (bad names, requirement, arguments or timeout), `limit-exceeded` (too many open calls, arguments too large), `not-permitted` (no `channels` permission), `stale-handle` (the player left); everything else comes back as the `service-result` event.

### `cancel-remote` <Badge type="info" text="function" />

```txt
cancel-remote: func(id: call-id) -> bool;
```

(0.3.1) Forgets an open remote call: no event is delivered for it. False if it was not open.

### `caller` <Badge type="info" text="function" />

```txt
caller: func() -> option<remote-caller>;
```

(0.3.1) The caller of the remote call being served right now (also inside services that provider calls), or none when `call-service` was reached from a local call.
